items.title: Democrat revenge plot against Elon Musk: Insiders reveal painful punishment they're planning after Texas humiliation...
items.summary:
Democrat revenge plot against Elon Musk: Insiders reveal painful punishment they're planning after Texas humiliation... and move that would make him turn on MAGA | Tom Leonard & Charlie Spiering, Daily Mail

When Elon Musk announced dramatically that he was moving the headquarters of SpaceX and X businesses out of California in July 2024, he revealed that the 'final straw' was the passage of a bill that banned schools from being forced to inform parents that they had a trans child.

'Because of this law and the many others that preceded it, attacking both families and companies, SpaceX will now move its HQ from Hawthorne, California, to Starbase, Texas,' Musk told his 54 million X followers to loud approval.

The message was clear: he was leaving the uber-woke, almost-broke Democrat nightmare of the Golden State for the conservative, low-regulation nirvana of the Lone Star state. And California would rue the day it forced out the world's richest man and his trillion-dollar business.

Well, let's just say it hasn't quite worked out as planned. Musk's new US Senator in Texas, James Talarico, has strong views on the trans issue, too: He has said that 'God is nonbinary' and, although he has now slightly backtracked, long opposed any restrictions on trans student athletes competing in girls' sports.

The billionaire who fled the Democrats running one state has now found himself surrounded by new ones about to run another, and the latest are not expected to go easy on one of their great tormentors.

As Texas broke 30 years of Republican rule in this week's Midterms, electing its first Democratic governor, Gina Hinojosa, in more than three decades and Talarico flipping the Senate seat for the Democrats for the first time since 1988, Musk's decision to move himself and his businesses there in a burst of Republican righteousness looks to have been just a little ill-timed.

In fact, some are asking whether Musk may not turn out to be one of the elections' biggest losers.

Not only has his conservative promised land turned overnight into – at least for now – a true blue bastion, but the carnage in the tech stock market two days after the election lost him billions, all while resurgent Democrats in Washington say he is high on the list of people they want to investigate.

It was surely no coincidence that shares of SpaceX tumbled 5.5 percent while Tesla – another trillion dollar plus company – was down 5.1 percent after the election shock – even as the markets generally went in the opposite direction.

However, it was hardly as if he hadn't seen it all coming. The billionaire owner of electric car maker Tesla, social media platform X and rocket-to-AI company SpaceX spent nearly half a billion dollars to support Republican candidates, of which $224 million was spent on Texas, mostly on Talarico's flawed and unpopular rival, Ken Paxton.

On election day, Musk urged his army of X followers to vote Republican but later deleted the post.

The midterms could now prove both a business and a personal nightmare for Musk, who has been baiting the Democrats for years and was Trump's biggest campaign donor in 2024.

Washington insiders familiar with senior Democrat thinking on Musk told the Daily Mail that there will be little appetite for any rapprochement with him.

'They view him as a class traitor,' said a source. 'Elon was once their green hero for pioneering electric cars and leading the charge for getting rid of fossil fuels and he betrayed them…They want to make him hurt.'

However, it's always said that money talks and Musk, estimated to be worth as much as $865 billion, may be able to buy his way back into Democrat affections, some believe.

The party has a significant fund-raising problem while Musk's politics are not as trenchant as he makes out - he donated cash to Barack Obama's campaigns and endorsed Hillary Clinton for president in 2016.

'I could 100 percent see Elon donating to Democrats again, depending on their outreach,' said another insider. 'He could easily flip back to a more favorable position if they are willing to work with him.'

For the moment, there is no sign of any friendliness between the two camps.

'Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,' Musk wrote sarcastically in a post on X early on Wednesday morning as the scale of the Republican defeat became clear.

'Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time,' he added a few minutes later, referencing unproven rumors that he interfered in Trump's successful 2024 election campaign.

After his ill-fated involvement in the Trump administration last year when, waving a chainsaw, he ran the chaotic DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) initiative to slash the size and cut of government costing 300,000 federal workers their jobs but barely curbed federal spending, Musk had stepped back from the political spotlight.

The DOGE farce, which Musk claimed in an interview last December was 'a little successful,' sparked violent anti-Tesla protests across the US and Europe in which cars were sometimes set on fire.

In the future, Musk may indeed find it easier doing business in low orbit than in Texas. The man who wants to colonize Mars may even want to consider moving there sooner rather than later.

That's unlikely given Musk has been putting roots down in Texas since 2020. After tiring of Covid-19 restrictions on the operation of his California Tesla factory, he announced he was moving the car company's HQ to Texas.

He also moved there personally, choosing the state capital of Austin, which he called a 'mini-California' (a compliment apparently) which would become 'the biggest boomtown that America has seen in a half-century.'

The billionaire, who has fathered at least 14 children with four women, developed a luxurious compound in a gated community in Austin, where he was able to house his various offspring and their mothers in separate but adjoining properties.

The adjoining homes, which Musk secretly bought for a total of $35 million, include a 14,400sq ft Tuscan-style villa and a six-bedroom mansion. When he visits, Musk stays at a third mansion a ten-minute walk away.

Meanwhile, Musk has come to rely heavily on Texas for the expansion of his business empire and even the fulfillment of his dreams of colonizing space.

He has already located Tesla's biggest US vehicle factory outside Austin while SpaceX launches its rockets into space from its Starbase complex in the southeastern corner of the state in Boca Chica near Brownsville. The rockets are also built in Texas, in Bastrop County.

All told, his companies employ more than 20,000 people in the Lone Star state.

And there were expected to be 3,000 more jobs when he opens a $16.8 billion Terafab chip plant elsewhere in the state, which SpaceX said it selected because of Texas's 'business-friendly climate.'

That money he has vested in Texas could earn him favor.

A Texas political strategist told the Daily Mail: 'There's no way Democrats want to completely crush Elon in Texas. He employs tens of thousands of people in Texas. He built an entire city there.'

However, he will no longer enjoy the full-scale access and perks that he had under business-friendly Republican governor Greg Abbott, sources said.

He was able to draw on $30 million of state funds for the Terafab project, which the company says will boast more than 100 million square feet of manufacturing space.

The chip plant will be a key ingredient of Musk's ambitious plans to develop the AI part of his empire.

However, those dreams rely on the state cooperating with him on the huge resources that AI needs in terms of electricity and water, as well as providing a benign regulatory climate in granting environmental permits and tax incentives.

Until now, he has been given pretty much all he desired in Texas. Not only was President Trump pro-AI but Musk had a warm relationship with Abbott. In 2020, Abbott promised Musk 'more freedom where he could expand the way he wanted to expand.' He later described Musk as 'the leading visionary of our time.'

You won't find incoming Democrat governor, Gina Hinojosa, saying anything like that. She shares the skepticism about AI and the ultra-wealthy Silicon Valley barons pushing it that is rife in her party.

Hinojosa campaigned not only against generous corporate subsidies but also against Musk himself.

She sued last month to obtain emails between Musk and Abbott, accusing the latter of selling out Texas by offering favorable deals to the billionaire. She also claimed Musk received $1.7 billion in state property tax breaks for his companies after he made a large donation to Abbott's re-election campaign.

In her victory speech on Tuesday night, Hinojosa didn't mention him by name but, along with other Democrat politicians nowadays, targeted billionaires for criticism.

'Does Texas belong to the people of Texas, or is this the billionaires' world and we just live in it?' she said to a crowd, raising loud cheers.

She pledged to take power from the 'powerful people who have gotten very comfortable running this state.' It seemed fairly obvious who she was likely thinking of.

Talarico also managed to attack Musk in his victory speech without specifically naming him. 'We must get big money out of our politics, so no billionaire or trillionaire can buy our elections,' he said. 'We must unrig this economic system that only benefits the top one percent.' There is only one trillionaire in the US.

Later, asked by Politico if he believed that Congress should investigate Musk, Talarico replied that 'obviously, there needs to be accountability for any wrongdoing.'

But he also said: 'What would be more helpful is getting big money out of our politics, banning corporate PACs, banning super PACs, so billionaires and trillionaires can't buy our elections.'

Talarico may feel it diplomatic not to be too openly hostile (not for the moment, at least) to a Texas employer as powerful as Musk but there's no love lost between the pair.

During the election campaign, Musk frequently savaged Talarico on social media, going personal as usual by calling him a 'far left extremist,' 'pure evil' and 'a creep.'

He also claimed the Democrat would 'abolish democracy,' 'open the borders' and 'will vote to trans your kids.'

'There is something deeply wrong with Talarico,' Musk mused ominously.

Talarico resisted the personal assaults in returning fire, but accused Musk of 'trying to buy Texas.' He told voters: 'Elon Musk wants our wants our land, he wants our water, he wants our taxpayer dollars and he wants his very own personal United States senator.'

With the young Democrat trouncing Paxton by more than 12 percent, it must be fair to assume that Musk has come out of this election with his reputation among many fellow Texans even lower than when he went into it.

Democrat state senator Nathan Johnson, the next Texas attorney general, showed just how much local politicians have come to loathe him, telling NBC on Wednesday that Musk was a 'cruel, arrogant, ignorant' person who has 'demonstrated his disregard for the public interest.'

Johnson said he had no intention of giving Musk the leeway he enjoyed under the outgoing Republican administration. He has already revealed he plans to investigate whether SpaceX unfairly benefited from a state grant program designed to improve rural broadband.

He went on: 'I don't have a hit list, but I show no deference to a guy who has gone to great lengths to control the government and do enormous damage globally.'

Commentators concur that the midterms represent not only a severe blow to Musk in Texas but also to his reputation nationally, as voters across the US expressed their contempt for billionaires assuming they can buy political influence.

'He is certainly the most visible of all these billionaire-trillionaires, and it put him on the ballot in a way that, I think, was difficult for a lot of people to swallow,' said Brandon Rottinghaus, a political science professor at the University of Houston of the part Musk played in Texas in the midterms.

'And it hurt Republicans because his presence really did, I think, magnify these concerns.'

JC Lintzenich, a visiting senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund, told CNBC's Squawk Box Europe that voters were repelled by billionaires throwing vast sums into getting an election outcome they desired. The results, he said, were 'clearly a rejection of the Elon Musk aspect that has found its way into the Trump orbit.'

Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management, predicted a 'Democratic sweep of Congress would put pressure on tech and potentially bring regulatory pressure on everything AI and possibly slow down the wild, wild west growth figures that we see daily and often take for granted.'

Like Trump, Musk loves to be a winner, but he may soon have bigger problems in Texas than a bruised ego.

His AI development plans depended on support from Trump's pro-tech administration and the generally business-friendly policies of defeated Abbott.

The Musk AI operation is largely centered around two mega data centers, Colossus and Colossus II, near Memphis but he wants to expand considerably into Texas.

Unhelpfully, Congress is now under the control of a party that shares the widespread public opposition to allowing huge data centers, an essential part of AI development, to spread unchecked across the US.

And that includes Texas governor elect Hinojosa, who has called for a moratorium on new data centers and an end to the industry's tax breaks. As in other states facing a data center invasion, she wants developers to cover their full electricity costs rather than suck power from an over-stretched grid and to provide assurances that local communities will be protected.

All of this, of course, would be a major blow for Musk, a man who takes setbacks badly. Ahead of its IPO in June, SpaceX told investors that AI could be a $28.5 trillion industry but that is not going to happen without the data centers.

Musk has been aggressively building data centers on greenfield sites inside his Starbase complex in Boca Chica but that could be opposed by Hinojosa who has opposed selling a 1,300-acre beachfront state park to SpaceX after it emerged that the Abbott administration had discussed a sale.

'Let me be clear: Texas is not for sale,' Hinojosa said last month. Analysts expect her say over tax incentives and permitting will be a major obstacle for Musk.

And Musk has problems with the Democrats that go well beyond Texas data centers.

Shortly before the midterms, a group of Silicon Valley House Democrats wrote to White House chief-of-staff Susie Wiles to demand an investigation into recent interruptions of Musk's militarily essential internet service in Ukraine.

Unexplained restrictions on Starshield, a military version of Starlink, disrupted crucial Ukrainian drone missions in October. Defense sources said the limits appeared overnight without advance warning.

Musk has claimed that, unlike Starlink, Starshield is controlled by the US government. However, the White House has offered a different version of events, saying Trump reportedly asked Musk to lift the restrictions on Starshield.

Just as they've expressed fears about his outsized role in US politics, Democrats have made clear they are deeply concerned about a private citizen like Musk having so much power during wartime.

The Democrats' letter to Wiles made clear that they intended to investigate him themselves if they won control in Congress. A Democrat-controlled Congress could, if it chose, hold up Musk's planned multi-trillion-dollar merger of Tesla and SpaceX for a long time.

'Live by the sword, die by the sword,' Musk posted on X last month in a bullish response to potential congressional probes. 'Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets.'

Tough talk but many, including insiders in his own companies, believe Musk has too much invested in Texas to risk falling out too badly with its Democrat leaders.

They certainly don't expect him to leave Texas for the foreseeable future.

Of course, if the locals there make life too difficult for him, he might have no option. But where? Although Americans are turning en masse against the ultra-wealthy, there was one bright spot for the latter this week.

A proposition that would have instituted the world's tax on billionaires was on course to be rejected. The state that decided against hammering them? California.

items.title: SoftBank shares jumped 13.9% in Tokyo today. Minutes after the close, it reported a $7.1 billion loss.
items.summary:
SoftBank shares jumped 13.9% in Tokyo today. Minutes after the close, it reported a $7.1 billion loss.

The stock went from ¥3,400 to ¥3,872. Then the July-September numbers came out: a net loss of ¥1.12 trillion. Analysts were expecting a ¥129 billion profit. It's SoftBank's first loss in almost two years, per Bloomberg.

The strange part is OpenAI. SoftBank's stake there is now worth $99.6 billion on paper. It has put in $64.6 billion, the last $10 billion in October. So the biggest bet looks fine. What hurt was everything around it: finance costs of ¥790.7 billion in six months, up 132%, and a $3.73 billion loss on equipment for US data-center projects.

In the video below, Bloomberg's Peter Elstrom in May. He calls OpenAI Masayoshi Son's "biggest bet ever," paid for partly by selling Nvidia stock and borrowing. People inside SoftBank worried he was "a little bit starstruck." And for all that money, Son doesn't have a seat on OpenAI's board.

My take: the OpenAI stake isn't the problem yet. It's a paper gain. The interest bill is real, and it's due every quarter, gain or no gain. Retail investors bought the legend this morning. The company reported the cost of funding it this afternoon.

Tomorrow Tokyo gets to price both.

Are the fans early again, or did they just buy the top of a $7 billion quarter?

This is what the dot-com bust looked like in week 1. A few budget cuts. One paused plant. Nobody called it a crisis.

items.title: 📢 HƯỚNG DẪN CÁCH ĐẨY TREND TRÊN X – DÀNH CHO COPTERBANK
items.summary:
📢 HƯỚNG DẪN CÁCH ĐẨY TREND TRÊN X – DÀNH CHO COPTERBANK

Để giúp hashtag và chủ đề của fandom có cơ hội lên xu hướng trên X, mọi người nên chú ý một số nguyên tắc sau:

I. HIỂU CÁCH X GHI NHẬN TƯƠNG TÁC

X không chỉ ghi nhận số lượng bài đăng mà còn đánh giá chất lượng nội dung, tốc độ tương tác và mức độ lan tỏa của chủ đề.

Có 4 yếu tố quan trọng:

- Tốc độ bùng nổ: Hashtag/chủ đề được nhắc đến nhiều trong một khoảng thời gian ngắn, đặc biệt là 30 phút – 6 giờ đầu.

- Tương tác thực: Ưu tiên bình luận có nội dung, quote tweet kèm ý kiến và những cuộc trò chuyện qua lại.

- Nội dung đa dạng: Hạn chế đăng ảnh, caption hoặc meme giống hệt nhau. Cùng một chủ đề nhưng nên có cách thể hiện khác nhau.

- Độ lan tỏa: Không chỉ giới hạn trong fandom mà cần thu hút tương tác từ những người dùng bên ngoài cộng đồng.

II. NHỮNG VIỆC NÊN LÀM KHI ĐĂNG BÀI

1. Luôn có nội dung đi kèm hashtag
   
   Không nên chỉ đăng hashtag. Hãy viết thêm nhận xét, cảm xúc, câu hỏi hoặc phân tích ngắn về chủ đề.
  Ví dụ:
   "Phân cảnh này trong phim thực sự khiến mình nổi da gà!"
   #.TenPhim

2. Ưu tiên nội dung gốc
   
Có thể đăng:
   
- Những đoạn clip được biên tập với cách thể hiện khác nhau.
   
- Ảnh hậu trường.
   
- Meme tự sáng tạo.
   
- Fanart với phong cách riêng.
   
   Hạn chế đăng lại cùng một bức ảnh hoặc một nội dung trên hàng loạt tài khoản.

3. Đăng bài tập trung theo khung giờ thống nhất
   
 - Thống nhất thời gian bắt đầu đẩy trend.
  
 - Tập trung đăng trong những đợt lớn thay vì đăng rải rác cả ngày.
  
 - Đặc biệt chú ý khoảng thời gian đầu khi chiến dịch bắt đầu.

4. Ưu tiên bình luận và quote tweet
   
   Thay vì chỉ thả tim hoặc chia sẻ, hãy:
   
- Quote bài đăng kèm nhận xét của riêng mình.
   
- Bình luận có nội dung.
   
- Trả lời bình luận của người khác để tạo thành cuộc trò chuyện tự nhiên.

5. Tránh spam tương tác
   
 - Không bình luận liên tục bằng những biểu tượng cảm xúc giống nhau.
  
 - Không copy nguyên caption của người khác.
 
 - Không đăng 10 bài liên tiếp có nội dung giống nhau.
  
 - Không chỉ retweet mà không kèm bất kỳ ý kiến nào.

6. Sử dụng hashtag hợp lý
   
 - Ưu tiên 1–2 hashtag chính.
  
 - Viết đúng chính tả và thống nhất cách sử dụng.
 
 - Không nhồi nhét quá nhiều hashtag trong một bài đăng.

III. NHỮNG ĐIỀU FANDOM CẦN TRÁNH

❌ Copy nguyên caption của nhau.

❌ Đăng hàng loạt bài có cùng nội dung, hình ảnh.

❌ Chỉ đăng ảnh kèm hashtag mà không có nội dung.

❌ Chỉ retweet liên tục mà không tạo tương tác.

❌ Spam biểu tượng cảm xúc hoặc bình luận giống nhau.

✅ Thay vào đó, hãy trò chuyện tự nhiên, đưa ra quan điểm cá nhân và đặt những câu hỏi gợi mở như:

- "Mọi người nghĩ sao về chi tiết này?"
- "Đây có phải là một hint mà chúng ta đã bỏ lỡ không?"

Đừng quên tương tác với cả những người ngoài fandom để chủ đề có cơ hội tiếp cận nhiều nhóm người dùng hơn.

IV. CHECKLIST ĐẨY TREND CHO FANDOM

🔥 TRƯỚC GIỜ G:

- Thống nhất hashtag sử dụng.
- Thống nhất thời gian đăng bài.
- Thống nhất chủ đề: cảnh phim, nhân vật hoặc thông điệp muốn lan tỏa.

🚀 TRONG 30–60 PHÚT ĐẦU:
Mỗi người có thể chủ động:

- Đăng ít nhất 1 bài viết gốc.
- Trả lời 2–3 bài đăng của người khác.
- Quote ít nhất 1 bài viết kèm ý kiến cá nhân.

📈 SAU ĐÓ:

- Tiếp tục quote và thảo luận những bài viết có nội dung tốt.
- Trả lời bình luận từ cả những người ngoài fandom.
- Duy trì cuộc trò chuyện một cách tự nhiên.

💗 ĐIỀU QUAN TRỌNG NHẤT:

Đẩy trend không đơn thuần là cuộc đua về số lượng bài đăng hay lượt thả tim. Điều quan trọng là tạo ra nhiều nội dung chất lượng, tương tác thực chất và giúp chủ đề được lan tỏa .

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?

The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

The AI trade has regained momentum despite — or maybe because of — Nvidia's struggles following the weekend revelations from CEO Jensen Huang.

The big picture: Monday's sudden burst of exuberance for AI was the latest wide swing for a market upended by last week's "blue tsunami" in the midterm elections and the threat they could pose to the data center boom. [...] "We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analysts wrote in a note Monday.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.
